description: I'm a Fullstack Developer specializing in Next.js, React, and 3D UI animations (GSAP, Three.js). You should join because we already have a crystal-clear SRS document, a solid tech architecture, and a winning roadmap! We are looking for Data Researchers (NASA datasets), 3D Artists, UI/UX Designers, and Video Editors/Storytellers.
summary: Beyond the Signal is an interactive 3D historical atlas exploring human-made equipment left on the Moon and Mars. Users can rotate and explore 3D planetary globes, discover documented spacecraft hardware at mapped locations, and uncover each artifact’s mission history, coordinates, timeline, final communication or mission ending, present status, and historical significance. The experience combines archival imagery, searchable artifact records, bilingual English and Bangla storytelling, and direct source links to connect every story with documented evidence. It helps students, educators, and space enthusiasts explore humanity’s lasting footprint beyond Earth.
details:
Over fifty years of robotic and crewed exploration have left dozens of historic rovers, landers, impactors, and scientific instruments resting across the Moon and Mars. Information about these artifacts is often scattered across dense technical archives, making it difficult for everyday learners—especially non-English speakers—to visualize where these missions happened and why they matter. Beyond the Signal bridges that gap by turning raw planetary coordinates and mission logs into an accessible, story-driven spatial experience.

How It Works :
Built as a full-stack interactive web application using React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Three.js / WebGL, Beyond the Signal renders rotatable 3D globes of the Moon and Mars overlaid with high-resolution planetary basemaps and interactive location pins.

Interactive 3D Exploration: Users can freely orbit, zoom, and switch between lunar and Martian surfaces, filtering artifacts by mission era, agency, or operational status (active, retired, or impact site).

Rich Artifact Provenance Cards: Selecting any pin opens a detailed dossier featuring mission timelines, exact selenographic or areographic coordinates, final telemetry/communication logs, archival photography, and direct links to official NASA mission records.

Bilingual Accessibility & Ambient Immersion: Every story and interface element supports instant toggling between English and Bangla, paired with subtle spatial ambient audio (cosmic-ambient) and keyboard-navigable controls to make space history engaging and inclusive.

What We'd Build Next :
In future iterations, we plan to integrate real-time NASA Deep Space Network (DSN) telemetry feeds for currently active missions, add an augmented reality (AR) tabletop mode for classrooms, and expand the catalog to include deep-space probes and orbital heritage sites across the solar system.
